editorial_contributions.text:
Summary: A subset \(A \subset \mathbb R^2\) is said to avoid distance \(1\) if: \( \forall x,y \in A, \left\| x-y \right\|_2 \neq 1\). In this paper we study the number \(m_1(\mathbb R^2)\) which is the supremum of the upper densities of measurable sets avoiding distance 1 in the Euclidean plane. Intuitively, \(m_1(\mathbb R^2)\) represents the highest proportion of the plane that can be filled by a set avoiding distance 1. This parameter is related to the fractional chromatic number \(\chi_f(\mathbb R^2)\) of the plane.

We establish that \(m_1(\mathbb R^2) \leq 0.25647\) and \(\chi_f(\mathbb R^2) \geq 3.8991\).
